title: The 8 Level of Sunday Scaries
house: A sprawling, neon-lit metropolis called Produce City where vegetable and fruit citizens commute in rusty yellow cabs, work frantic desk jobs, and panic about Monday mornings under towering glowing digital billboards.
catchphrase: The glowing digit on your forehead never lies.
links: The bitter lemon barista in Level 1 mentions a quiet blueberry man who always leaves a huge tip.
The exhausted broccoli accountant in Level 3 spots a sleek green grape sports car speeding past the bus stop.
The glowing coconut tech bro in Level 8 sips espresso at the exact same cafe where the orange starts her shift.

levels.open_loop: Why did the glowing bank notification make her Sunday night instantly freeze?

gegenspieler.tat: Laughs at her for checking her pitiful bank balance on the subway and kicks her spilled coffee away.

levels.name: Ruby, 22, Intern
levels.story: The 8 Level of Sunday Scaries. Level 1. 12 dollars in my checking account and Sunday night terror is already clawing at my throat. My strawberry skin is pale, my cheap polyester thrift jacket smells like stale subway air, and the glowing '12 $' on my forehead flashes like a neon warning sign. I am staring at my phone in the dim kitchen of my mouse-infested Brooklyn apartment, watching the clock tick toward 7:00 AM Monday. My phone buzzes with a rent reminder from my landlord. A crisp, expensive bell chimes behind me. You can't even afford a decent cup of instant noodles for dinner, can you? My hands tremble against the kitchen counter, my heart slamming against my ribs as I realize I have no money for tomorrow's commute. The screen lights up with a sudden, terrifying alert from my bank app. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Leo, 28, Barista
levels.story: The 8 Level of Sunday Scaries. Level 2. 2,400 dollars a month in tips and rent is due in exactly three hours. My lemon skin is sour and peeling, my stained green apron smells like burnt espresso beans, and my glowing forehead display reads '2,400 $'. I am wiping down the sticky counter of the downtown cafe while outside, the relentless Sunday evening drizzle washes over the gray asphalt. My phone buzzes on the metal prep table. A sleek, perfectly polished blueberry man in a cashmere turtleneck walks in, his forehead flashing '12,500 $'. Is this lukewarm foam the best your miserable minimum-wage hands can manage? My teeth grind together as I bite back a bitter retort, my hands clenching into tight fists against the espresso machine. The cafe bell chimes again, and a blinding light erupts from my phone screen as an urgent message arrives from my manager. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Broccoli Bob, 34, Accountant
levels.story: The 8 Level of Sunday Scaries. Level 3. 4,900 dollars a month and I am still eating instant mac and cheese while staring at a mountain of spreadsheets at 11:00 PM on Sunday. My broccoli floret head is drooping with sheer exhaustion, my beige office button-down is wrinkled, and my glowing forehead reads '4,900 $'. I am sitting in my sterile cubicle on the 40th floor, the fluorescent lights buzzing like angry wasps. A tall, immaculate dragonfruit executive in a sharp Italian suit strides down the empty corridor, his forehead gleaming with '38,000 $'. Finish these tax audits by 8:00 AM or find a new box to sleep in, he mutters without even breaking his stride. My jaw tightens so hard my teeth ache, a sudden wave of hot fury flooding my green veins. I reach out to push the folder away, but my desk phone suddenly starts flashing a bright red light. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Valencia, 41, Manager
levels.story: The 8 Level of Sunday Scaries. Level 4. 8,400 dollars a month and I still spend my Sunday nights vomiting from sheer corporate anxiety in the executive washroom. My orange peel skin is taut and polished, my pearl necklace feels like a heavy chain, and my glowing forehead proudly displays '8,400 $'. I am standing on the polished marble balcony of my penthouse apartment, looking down at the tiny toy cars crawling along the wet highway below. My phone rings with an urgent call from regional headquarters. A mysterious, silver coconut tycoon in a bespoke tuxedo steps out of the private elevator lobby, his forehead glowing with an blinding '95,000 $'. Don't bother prepping the quarterly report, Valencia, someone else is taking your desk tomorrow, he whispers with an ice-cold smile. My blood runs instantly cold, my breath catches in my throat, and my fingers loosen around my smartphone. The screen flashes a catastrophic system notification. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Indigo, 29, Director
levels.story: The 8 Level of Sunday Scaries. Level 5. 12,500 dollars a month in base pay and I spent my entire Sunday night hiding in my home office because I'm terrified my team will find out I have no idea what I'm doing. My blueberry skin is smooth and navy-blue, my cashmere turtleneck is spotless, and my glowing forehead reads '12,500 $'. I am pacing across the hardwood floor of my luxury loft, listening to the heavy rain beat against the floor-to-ceiling windows. My laptop screen displays a flashing red alert from our financial software. A chaotic young lemon intern bursts through my office door without knocking, his forehead flashing '2,400 $'. You think your fancy title protects you from the crash, but the board just voted to wipe our department out! he shouts, spilling lukewarm coffee across my imported Persian rug. My chest tightens into a suffocating knot, my breath hitching as I stare at the ruined rug. My phone lights up with a direct call from the CEO. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Melon, 37, VP
levels.story: The 8 Level of Sunday Scaries. Level 6. 22,000 dollars a month and I am sitting in my dark leather armchair at 2:00 AM on Sunday, shaking because my empire is about to crumble. My watermelon skin is striped dark green and smooth, my velvet blazer is impeccably tailored, and my glowing forehead displays '22,000 $'. I am holding a glass of aged scotch while staring at the glowing security monitors of my corporate headquarters. A tired broccoli accountant in a wrinkled shirt steps out of the shadows near my private study, his forehead flashing '4,900 $'. I just sent the forensic audit straight to the federal regulators, Melon, your little Sunday game is over, he says with a cold, unforgiving smirk. My hand jerks, sending the crystal scotch glass shattering against the marble floor, amber liquid pooling like blood. My heart hammers like a sledgehammer against my ribs. My encrypted phone rings with an unknown caller ID. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Pitaya, 45, CEO
levels.story: The 8 Level of Sunday Scaries. Level 7. 38,000 dollars a month and I am locked inside my private airport hangar at 4:00 AM on Sunday, watching my entire life unravel over a secure satellite phone. My dragonfruit skin is vibrant magenta with green-tipped bracts, my silk scarf is blowing in the hangar draft, and my glowing forehead reads '38,000 $'. I am standing beside my idling private jet while rain pounds against the corrugated metal roof. A cunning watermelon executive in a velvet blazer steps out from behind the landing gear, her forehead flashing '22,000 $'. The federal marshals already have your asset list, Pitaya, your private jet isn't going anywhere tonight, she says with a chilling, victorious laugh. My blood turns to ice, my grip tightening around the satellite phone until my knuckles turn white. A sudden flashing red siren illuminates the entire runway outside. A black armored car tears through the security gates. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: Cocco, 52, Founder
levels.story: The 8 Level of Sunday Scaries. Level 8. 95,000 dollars a month and I walked away from it all at 5:00 AM on Sunday just to sit on a lonely park bench in the rain. My coconut shell head is hard and brown, my custom tuxedo is soaked through, and my glowing forehead reads '95,000 $'. I am watching the sun finally break over Produce City, painting the glass skyscrapers in shades of cold gold. A young strawberry intern with wet petals and a forehead flashing '12 $' walks past, pausing to look at me with tired, knowing eyes. You built an entire city of numbers that only make us run in circles, don't you ever feel tired of counting? she asks softly, handing me a small, warm paper cup of black coffee. My hard outer shell cracks just a fraction, a genuine smile touching my lips for the first time in decades. I reach into my pocket, pull out my glowing digital badge, and lay it gently on the wooden bench between us. The numbers flicker, fade to black, and for the first time in my life, the Sunday Scaries are entirely gone. What number will show on your forehead when the clock strikes Monday morning?
